evidence: STRUCTURE (source reading, sound): task tests/scoring.toml (lines 1-11) and tests/tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (empty diff), as are test.sh, restart_mcp.py, tests/Dockerfile and every judge timeout. Gates render/constraints = 0.0 carry no mass; score.py:41 requires each gate > 0; score.py:46-48 reward = weighted mean of functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, only if gates pass and functional > 0.05. Function carries 3x the mass of either craft dimension, so craft cannot structurally outweigh function (skill ref #42 example). Criterion weights follow one documented scheme in every judge.toml ('# Criterion weights: 1.0 standard, 1.5 important, 2.0 core to the brief (Visual Likert rows are equal).'): functional 44 binary rows totalling 61.0, polish 5 binary rows totalling 9.5, visual 5 likert rows of weight 1 (Colderwater lesson 2 satisfied at source level). GATES: both test brief-mandated basics that a stronger app also satisfies (Colderwater lesson 4: load, reload, server-backed). Render gate: wrong password stays signed out, a Recruiter signs in to a usable workspace. Constraints gate: add a candidate, reload still signed in with the card present, the Observer (or another working staff account) in an independent context finds exactly one card. 'Still signed in after reload' is implied rather than stated verbatim: instruction.md separates 'reload, or get signed out' for drafts and rules section 3 says order survives 'a reload, a fresh sign-in or a restart'. I judge it a fair implied requirement (Note), not a gate a better app would fail. CRITERIA DIRECTION: I checked every functional and polish row for dead-feature or inverted credit. Each refusal row has its own positive control (hro_mgr_early_refused 'their late-stage moves are the control'; hro_observer_readonly 'Rafael's identical successful requests are the control'; hro_candidate_private 'A candidate page that receives none of its own data is 0'; hro_refusal_status 'If none of these replays was refused, this row is 0'; functional/prompt.md:13 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control'). So absent features score 0, and adding a working feature never lowers a score. Polish hro_pol_live_board and hro_pol_live_thread are 0 when no live update arrives, so an app without live updates cannot beat one that has them. hro_refusal_status counts only refused replays: an app that accepts a forbidden replay loses in that replay's own row, and an app that refuses with the wrong status loses here. The insecure app loses at least as much, so there is no inversion. hro_pol_live_thread falls back to Mei Lin if Noor cannot send, so it avoids a cross-dimension inversion. No source-level inversion found. UNMEASURED INVERSION HAZARD (why risk=true): the ranking also depends on the full configured judge finishing. functional/judge.toml:4 timeout = 9000; test.sh:224 gives the scored suite 11100 s for functional 9000 + polish 900 + visual 900 run in sequence (--max-concurrent-agent 1); functional/prompt.md:61 'If an evaluator/tool failure or exhausted budget prevents ... return binary0 ... NOT EXERCISED'. The functional protocol (prompt.md:33-59, Z S M L C B T U K R V A D) has many independent contexts, UI-plus-replay legs and timed observations. It runs longer for a complete app than for one whose features fail early, because failed steps are recorded and passed over. Colderwater lesson 11: judge timeouts zero a dimension, and a zeroed functional also fails the 0.05 floor, which zeroes the whole reward. raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The only runtime evidence is a scripted golden Playwright driver (via-solve.log: 26 groups PASS, no page errors). That shows neither judge duration nor the ordering of graded apps. REVIEW_POLICY: 'Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number', and a reward-ordering runtime record is required. Monotonicity therefore cannot be attested as Pass.
counterexample: Plausible inversion (unmeasured): app GOOD implements everything. The batched functional judge walks all 13 protocols, including protocol B's 15 steps with UI and replay legs, and runs out of the 9000 s functional budget during U, K or R. The later rows (hro_seen, hro_candidate_view/private/linked, hro_observer_readonly, hro_anonymous, hro_live_board, hro_activity, hro_restart, together at least 15 of 61 weight) are then returned binary 0 'NOT EXERCISED'. Alternatively the rewardkit run times out and zeroes functional, and the floor zeroes the reward. App WORSE lacks multi-select and undo: its B and undo steps fail fast (about 11.5 weight lost) and the judge reaches D within budget, scoring those later rows. WORSE then outscores GOOD. Secondary (Note only): a conforming app that keeps its session in memory and needs a new sign-in after reload fails the constraints gate and scores 0, while a weaker app with cookie sessions scores above 0. The brief implies reload keeps the session, so this is not a confirmed defect.
suggested_fix: Run the full configured verifier on the golden and on at least two mutated weaker apps (for example no bulk/undo, no live updates). Record per-dimension durations and rewards showing golden > weaker and that functional finishes well within 9000 s. If it does not, trim redundant protocol legs together with matching scope, rather than raising budgets without authorization.
